item.title: STF exclui ISS de base de cálculo das contribuições federais, em vitória para empresas
item.description: O plenário do Supremo Tribunal Federal formou nesta quarta-feira maioria contrária à inclusão do ISS, o imposto municipal sobre serviços, da base de cálculo do PIS e da Cofins, contribuições federais criadas para financiar a seguridade social.
item.dc:creator: Ricardo Brito
item.content:encoded: O plenário do Supremo Tribunal Federal formou nesta quarta-feira maioria contrária à inclusão do ISS, o imposto municipal sobre serviços, da base de cálculo do PIS e da Cofins, contribuições federais criadas para financiar a seguridade social. O governo calcula que o impacto potencial da decisão desta quarta-feira é de R$34,5 bilhões. A decisão representa uma vitória para empresas que pleiteavam a retirada do ISS das contribuições federais e uma derrota para o governo federal, que estimava um impacto de dezenas de bilhões em caso de derrota. Empatado até então em cinco votos a cinco, o julgamento foi retomado nesta quarta-feira e contou com o voto decisivo do ministro Luiz Fux, que acompanhou o voto do ministro aposentado Celso de Mello e se manifestou a favor da tese das empresas. Fux chegou a propor uma modulação dos efeitos da decisão, mas os ministros decidiram aguardar a apresentação de eventuais embargos de declaração sobre os efeitos do julgamento. Procurada pela reportagem, a Procuradoria-Geral da Fazenda Nacional (PGFN) disse estar "analisando a decisão do Supremo Tribunal Federal para definir a estratégia de atuação". VITÓRIA A EMPRESAS O advogado tributarista Leonardo Roesler, sócio do RCA Advogados, disse que a decisão do STF recoloca um limite na relação entre arrecadação e atividade econômica, representando uma vitória a empresas prestadoras de serviços. "Agora, o alcance temporal do julgamento merece tanta atenção quanto a vitória de mérito. A recuperação de valores depende dos termos da decisão, de eventual modulação, da prescrição e da situação processual de cada contribuinte. Não se pode anunciar uma devolução automática dos últimos cinco anos para todas as empresas", disse. "É necessário examinar os recolhimentos, a documentação e os procedimentos cabíveis para restituição ou compensação, inclusive o trânsito em julgado quando exigido para compensar créditos reconhecidos judicialmente. A aplicação do precedente exige precisão quanto à tese fixada, aos regimes abrangidos e à comprovação contábil dos valores", explicou. Para a Flávio Molinari, sócio da área tributária do Collavini Borges Molinari Advogados, a decisão deve ser "festejada", principalmente levando em consideração que o STF já tinha decidido que o imposto estadual ICMS não compõe a base de cálculo da PIS e da Cofins, no chamado Tema 69, em 2017. Além disso, no início do mês, o tribunal também decidiu que [USN:L1N45T10Q TEXT:"créditos"] fiscais presumidos de ICMS não podem ser incluídos na base de cálculo de PIS/Cofins. "Evidentemente, tem um impacto orçamentário que provavelmente vai provocar um pedido de modulação de efeitos via embargos de declaração pela Procuradoria da Fazenda Nacional. E esse ponto vai inaugurar um novo capítulo ainda nessa discussão", afirmou Molinari.

item.title: Rice rescues Arsenal at Bayern as Real Madrid hit four
item.description: Declan Rice rescued Arsenal with a late equaliser in an electric 2-2 Champions League draw at Bayern Munich on Wednesday, while Real Madrid beat RB Leipzig 4-1 and Como handed Manchester United a bruising defeat by the same score.
item.dc:creator: Fernando Kallas
item.content:encoded: Declan Rice rescued Arsenal with a late equaliser in an electric 2-2 Champions League draw at Bayern Munich on Wednesday, while Real Madrid beat RB Leipzig 4-1 and Como handed Manchester United a bruising defeat by the same score. Arsenal's evening in Germany began ominously when Bukayo Saka limped out of the contest in the 10th minute, clutching his knee after falling while attempting a pass. Fifteen minutes later, however, Eberechi Eze raced on to Martin Odegaard's long ball and fired an angled shot past Manuel Neuer. Initially flagged offside, the goal was awarded following a VAR review. Bayern replied in the 35th minute when Harry Kane released Alphonso Davies down the left with a through ball from halfway, the Canadian breaking clear before beating David Raya with a composed right-footed finish. Kane put the hosts ahead from the penalty spot in the 61st minute after his shot struck Jurrien Timber's raised hand, blasting his 58th Champions League goal into the roof of the net. But Rice had the final say eight minutes from time, exchanging passes with Viktor Gyokeres inside the box before slotting past Neuer. COURTOIS KEEPS REAL AFLOAT At the Santiago Bernabeu, Real's emphatic scoreline owed much to goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois, who denied Romulo's close-range volley and thwarted Christopher Nkunku one-on-one before the hosts found their rhythm. Bernardo Silva broke the deadlock in the 43rd minute, pouncing to tap home almost on the goalline after Leipzig goalkeeper Maarten Vandevoordt spilled Federico Valverde's shot. Arda Guler doubled the lead seven minutes after halftime, beating a defender to Kylian Mbappe's goalbound header from Jude Bellingham's cross. Mbappe curled a shot into the top corner in the 83rd minute before Tidiam Gomis pulled one back a minute later. Substitute Yan Diomande capped Real's victory with a spectacular volley from Brahim Diaz's cross. Elsewhere, Galatasaray won 4-2 at Lille, Inter Milan edged Shakhtar Donetsk 1-0, Aston Villa beat Viking Stavanger 3-1 and Real Betis beat Feyenoord 1-0, while LASK stunned Sporting 3-2 in Lisbon. Paris St Germain, Aston Villa, Real Madrid, Liverpool and Real Betis top the standings having all made perfect starts to their Champions League campaigns, with three wins from three matches. Inter Milan overcame Alessandro Bastoni's dismissal to beat Shakhtar Donetsk, Carlos Augusto controlling Henrikh Mkhitaryan's long pass in his stride before scoring the 77th-minute winner. Bastoni had received a second booking eight minutes earlier for pushing an opponent away from the ball. Aston Villa comfortably beat Norway's Viking, Ross Barkley heading the opener from a corner before Emiliano Buendia converted a penalty and Alysson found the net with a deflected shot. Peter Christiansen struck Viking's late consolation. Isco's 59th-minute penalty following a handball gave Real Betis victory over Feyenoord in Seville, while Club Brugge beat Lens 3-0 through goals from Hans Vanaken, Joaquin Seys and Carlos Forbs. LASK stunned Sporting, recovering from Luis Suarez's early penalty with goals from Christoph Lang, Sasa Kalajdzic and Krystof Danek. Suarez scored again in the 89th minute but the hosts could not salvage a point. PAZ PUNISHES UNITED Earlier, Nico Paz tormented Manchester United with two goals and an assist as Como swept to victory in northern Italy, while Galatasaray won a six-goal thriller at Lille. Paz put Como ahead inside two minutes with a curling effort from the edge of the box, then helped double the lead four minutes after halftime, threading a perfectly weighted pass through for Anastasios Douvikas to finish first time past the advancing goalkeeper. The Argentine then robbed Carlos Baleba near the right touchline and surged diagonally for more than 30 metres before steering a left-footed finish inside the far post. Jacobo Ramon headed Como's fourth from substitute Kaiki Bruno's cross in the 76th minute, with Joshua Zirkzee grabbing United's stoppage-time consolation from Amad Diallo's delivery. In France, Galatasaray recovered from surrendering an early lead to beat Lille 4-2. Yunus Akgun fired the visitors ahead shortly after kickoff, but Soriba Diaoune equalised five minutes later and struck again in the 39th minute to put Lille in front. Alexey Batrakov headed Galatasaray level in the 44th minute before Lucas Torreira appeared to glance home a corner in the 52nd, although the effort was later credited as a Nabil Bentaleb own goal. Victor Osimhen completed the scoring nine minutes later with a powerful strike from the edge of the box.

item.title: US orders diplomats to depart Saudi Arabia amid Houthi strikes
item.description: The US State Department has ordered some diplomats and family members to depart from its missions in Saudi Arabia and plans to withdraw family members from a number of other US missions in the region, US officials told Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Rami Ayyub, Humeyra Pamuk, Timour Azhari
item.content:encoded: The US State Department has ordered some diplomats and family members to depart from its missions in Saudi Arabia and plans to withdraw family members from a number of other US missions in the region, US officials told Reuters. The order came as attacks in Saudi Arabia killed at least one person and injured eight others at a civilian airport in Dammam and two people were killed in a [USN:L1N46710X TEXT:"drone attack on an oil field"]. State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott said in a post on X that the department ordered the departure of "non-emergency US government employees and their family members in Saudi Arabia only" amid [USN:L1N4610L5 TEXT:"attacks by the Iran-aligned Houthis"] in Yemen on civilian targets in the country. Washington had returned some diplomatic personnel to the region in recent months after many were pulled out when Tehran launched attacks on US facilities after the US-Israeli war on Iran began in late February. "Iranian-supported Houthis have increasingly engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure resulting in civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions," Pigott said. Four US officials told Reuters that US missions in other Gulf states would also be ordering family members to leave. Pigott did not address changes to other missions outside Saudi Arabia. The latest withdrawals follow an escalation of the fighting in Yemen, opening another front in the regional conflict triggered by the US-Israeli war on Iran. The wider conflict has snarled global energy trade and hurt Gulf economies. After the departure order, Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority reported an attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam that killed one person and injured eight others. Earlier in the day, two people were killed after Saudi air defences intercepted a drone that was attempting to hit a facility at Saudi Aramco's Shaybah oilfield, the energy ministry said. The US embassy in Riyadh issued a security alert on Wednesday about possible further attacks by the Houthis on Saudi Arabia, after recent deadly strikes including [USN:S8N43T03L TEXT:"on Riyadh's airport"]. The embassy and a CIA station hosted there [USN:L1N3ZR1EN TEXT:"came under attack"] by drones in early March, as Iran began launching attacks across the region.

item.title: New Mexico sues to stop payouts to Jeffrey Epstein's lawyer, accountant
item.description: New Mexico has filed a civil lawsuit to block payments from Jeffrey Epstein's estate to the late sex offender's lawyer and accountant, and to recover damages for survivors of his alleged sexual abuse, the state's top law enforcement official said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Hay
item.content:encoded: New Mexico has filed a civil lawsuit to block payments from Jeffrey Epstein's estate to the late sex offender's lawyer and accountant, and to recover damages for survivors of his alleged sexual abuse, the state's top law enforcement official said on Wednesday. The suit is the first law enforcement action against Epstein's longtime personal attorney Darren Indyke and accountant Richard Kahn, according to New Mexico Attorney General Raul Torrez. The lawsuit alleges Indyke and Kahn facilitated, financed, and concealed Epstein's sex trafficking operation, including at his ranch 30 miles south of New Mexico's capital Santa Fe. They are co-executors of Epstein's estate, valued at $107 million, and respectively eligible for bequests of $50 million and $25 million from it, according to the complaint. Daniel Weiner, a lawyer representing Indyke and Kahn, rejected allegations the two "knowingly" facilitated Epstein's abuse of women, saying the crimes took place "behind closed doors, in secluded locations" when neither was present. The suit will test whether authorities are able to pin down allegations that a network of people and financial arrangements helped sustain and conceal Epstein's operations. “Jeffrey Epstein did not operate alone, and his death does not end the pursuit of accountability for the people who helped make his crimes possible,” Torrez said at a press conference in Albuquerque. He was joined by two survivors of Epstein's alleged abuse, Julia Molchanova and Anouska De Georgiou. Indyke and Kahn have already been named in civil lawsuits against the Epstein estate, including a complaint last month seeking damages for people pictured in the late financier's [USN:L6N45814E TEXT:"collection"] of child sexual abuse material. "Not a single woman has ever accused Mr. Indyke or Mr. Kahn of committing sexual abuse or witnessing sexual abuse," Weiner said in a statement, adding that the New Mexico attorney general's office had made no effort to interview the men before filing the lawsuit. New Mexico's civil action comes after the Democratic-run state in February [USN:L6N3ZF16Q TEXT:"reopened"] an investigation into activities at Epstein's Zorro Ranch in New Mexico, where he is accused of abusing women and girls for nearly three decades. Eight months into the probe, New Mexico has yet to file any criminal charges. The state has [USN:L6N442109 TEXT:"sued"] the US Department of Justice for access to unredacted files on Epstein, accusing the Trump administration of stonewalling its investigation. The DOJ said it provided some files but was [USN:L6N43H116 TEXT:"prevented"] from handing over most material due to privacy protections. Molchanova and De Georgiou, both prominent survivors of Epstein's sex trafficking network, applauded the New Mexico lawsuit to stop Indyke and Kahn profiting any further from the late sex-offender's estate. "Accountability cannot end with Epstein and Maxwell, it must extend to those who knowingly made their abuse possible, especially those who stand to profit from it," said De Georgiou, a key witness at the trial of Epstein's partner Ghislaine Maxwell, convicted and sentenced to 20 years in prison in 2022 for sex trafficking of a minor and related conspiracy.

item.title: Chevron to sharpen US Gulf focus with sale of older assets
item.description: Chevron is exploring the sale of some of its older oil and gas assets in the US Gulf, the company confirmed to Reuters, part of an effort to focus on high-growth developments in the region.
item.dc:creator: David French, Sheila Dang
item.content:encoded: Chevron (CVX.N) is exploring the sale of some of its older oil and gas assets in the US Gulf, the company confirmed to Reuters, part of an effort to focus on high-growth developments in the region. The energy producer is in the early stages of a multi-month process that could see a number of assets offloaded, a Chevron spokesperson said in response to questions from Reuters about the sale effort. "We are initiating the process of marketing some of our mature Gulf of America producing assets, including Petronius, Tubular Bells, and Llano as well as working interest in several other operated and non-operated fields," the spokesperson said. The move is part of Chevron's efforts to ensure its portfolio aligns with the company's priorities, the spokesperson said, adding there was no guarantee that sales would take place. With Chevron targeting production from the US Gulf to grow to 300,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day by the end of this year, the portfolio-trimming efforts indicate Chevron is increasingly focused on newer projects and opportunities in the region. This would include [USN:L1N3JZ01X TEXT:"Anchor"], its first platform producing at ultra-high subsea pressure, and Ballymore, which began production last year. The company is also pursuing exploration to find oil and gas resources near existing facilities, and has been a [USN:L1N3ZZ0X3 TEXT:"top spender"] in recent sales of drilling rights in the US Gulf conducted by the Interior Department. SHARPENING FOCUS Market conditions are favorable for Chevron's pruning efforts. There continues to be heightened buyer interest in American energy production, and asset valuations are supported by elevated oil prices -- US crude touched a six-month high on Tuesday. The sales will likely raise around $1 billion for the company, said two people aware of the sale effort, who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss confidential deliberations. Buyer interest is expected to come from international operators that specialize in offshore development and that are seeking to grow their US Gulf footprint, as well as US companies focused on the basin. Other energy majors may also show interest, the sources added. Petronius began producing in 2000, and Tubular Bells in 2014, according to Chevron's website. The company owns 100% of Tubular Bells, having initially held 43% but assumed the rest following its takeover of Hess. Chevron operates Petronius with Talos Energy (TALO.N) as its partner in the platform. Chevron's 50% position in Llano was also inherited from Hess. Production from the play, which is operated by Shell (SHEL.L) , started in 2004.

item.title: CVC explores deal to take Verisure private a year after IPO, FT reports
item.description: Buyout firm CVC is exploring a bid to take Swedish security firm Verisure private, the Financial Times reported on Wednesday, less than a year after private equity firm Hellman & Friedman floated the company in Stockholm.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Buyout firm CVC (CVC.AS) is exploring a bid to take Swedish security firm Verisure (VSURE.ST) private, the Financial Times reported on Wednesday, less than a year after private equity firm Hellman & Friedman floated the company in Stockholm. Here are some details: Verisure, which provides professionally monitored security services across 18 countries in Europe and Latin America, was listed in October 2025 at a valuation of 13.7 billion euros ($15.39 billion) The company's market value has since fallen to about 9.7 billion euros, according to LSEG data, with its shares down more than 33% so far this year Reuters could not immediately verify the report, while Verisure and CVC declined to comment CVC's interest is at an early stage and there is no certainty a deal will materialise, the report said Hellman & Friedman remains Verisure's largest shareholder with a 43.62% stake, LSEG data show ($1 = 0.8898 euros)

item.title: Meta ordered to pay $25 billion penalty to New Mexico in data privacy case
item.description: The ruling came in a case stemming from allegations that Cambridge Analytica, a British political consulting firm involved in Donald Trump's 2016 presidential campaign, obtained data from millions of Facebook users without their consent.
item.dc:creator: Diana Jones
item.content:encoded: A judge in New Mexico ordered Meta Platforms (META.O) on Wednesday to pay the state $25 billion after [USN:L6N45F10O TEXT:"a jury found"] the company had misled consumers about the privacy of their data, hitting the company with one of the largest financial penalties in US history. The ruling came in a case stemming from allegations that Cambridge Analytica, a British political consulting firm involved in Donald Trump's 2016 presidential campaign, obtained data from millions of Facebook users without their consent. New Mexico had sued Meta, accusing it of lying to Facebook users in New Mexico about who had access to their data. "Facebook's wrongdoing — over the course of years and systematically broadcast to the public — goes to the heart of Facebook's core business practices," Judge Francis Mathew wrote in his order, which came more than three weeks after the verdict. Mathew found that a penalty of more than $219 billion was warranted based on state law, but he reduced the figure to $25 billion. In a statement, C.J. Mahoney, Meta's chief legal officer, said the company is confident it will win on appeal. “This ruling, and the Attorney General's approach to this enforcement, makes it all but impossible to do business in the state of New Mexico," Mahoney said. "At its core, this lawsuit seeks to impose a tax on speech to enforce new rules for what people can say online." New Mexico Attorney General Raúl Torrez said in a statement after the ruling the penalty was one of the largest financial penalties against a corporation in US history. Meta previously faced [USN:KCN1UJ1L9 TEXT:"a $5 billion penalty"] from the US Federal Trade Commission in 2019 over the Cambridge Analytica scandal. Six other states settled their lawsuits against Meta related to Cambridge Analytica for $459.2 million as part of a [USN:L6N44N0VA TEXT:"$17.1 billion multistate settlement"] the company reached in August to resolve states' claims that the company's platforms had harmed teen mental health. LAWSUIT FILED FIVE YEARS AGO New Mexico's attorney general sued Meta in 2021 following revelations that Cambridge Analytica had [USN:L1N33D09I TEXT:"harvested personal data"] from as many as 87 million Facebook users through a third-party app. The state accused Meta of lying to Facebook users in New Mexico about who had access to their data and its handling of hate speech and misinformation posted on the platform. It alleged the company knew third parties had broad access to users' data and tolerated hate speech or other harmful content when it benefited the company's bottom line. Cambridge Analytica, now defunct, used the data for voter profiling and targeting. "It has been a long time coming holding Big Tech accountable," Torrez told a press conference in Albuquerque after Wednesday's ruling. "I think today's judgment is a clear break with that past and a very clear warning to those in this space and beyond that we intend to protect our people and protect our consumers." Mathew's decision comes as Meta faces thousands of lawsuits and pressure from lawmakers over the impact of Instagram and Facebook on teen mental health, with another trial slated to begin next week. Earlier this year, New Mexico won $942 million in a [USN:L6N4431IA TEXT:"pair of"] [USN:L6N40B0XV TEXT:"trials"] against Meta over claims it facilitated sexual exploitation of young people on Instagram and Facebook and misled consumers about the platforms' safety. Analyst Gil Luria, head of technology research at D.A. Davidson & Co, called the latest New Mexico ruling costly but unlikely to impact the company's value. "Meta is worth nearly two trillion dollars, and will likely continue to appeal these cases and drag them out," Luria said. EXPERTS EXPECT LONG APPEAL FIGHT Jurors in September had found that the company and its leadership made 26 misleading statements on data privacy, hate speech and other subjects. Multiplying those statements by their potential audience, they said the company had committed more than 43 million violations of New Mexico’s consumer protection laws. At a hearing on October 1, Randi McGinn, a lawyer for New Mexico, had asked Mathew to award the state between $35 billion and $40 billion. "This court should speak to Meta in the only language it understands, which is money, and the value of its stock price," McGinn said. In court filings, Meta urged Mathew to cap the penalties at $3.45 billion. The evidence showed that Meta does not sell user data and New Mexico did not prove that any consumer had actually been misled, the company said in court filings.

item.title: PETA urges Crystal Palace to retire bald eagle mascot Phoenix
item.description: Animal rights group PETA has urged Crystal Palace to retire its American bald eagle mascot, Phoenix, saying football stadiums are unsuitable environments that can distress birds and potentially put them and spectators at risk.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Animal rights group PETA has urged Crystal Palace to retire its American bald eagle mascot, Phoenix, saying football stadiums are unsuitable environments that can distress birds and potentially put them and spectators at risk. Palace, known as the Eagles since 1973, introduced a live eagle as a matchday mascot in 2010. Phoenix made her official debut in August 2024 at four months old, succeeding long-serving mascot Kayla, who died in 2020. In a letter to Palace CEO Sharon Lacey, People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals cited incidents involving birds at sporting events, including one in which a Charlton Athletic fan was found guilty of attempting to punch Kayla at a 2015 League Cup match. "A bright stadium filled with boisterous fans is no place for animals. Under such conditions, birds easily become frightened, disoriented, and panicked - placing themselves and others at risk...," PETA wrote. "When eagles are used for displays and entertainment, they are denied the opportunity to engage in their natural behaviour, resulting in frustration and stress. Wildlife doesn't belong in a football stadium... "Bald eagles are widely recognised as symbols of freedom. They deserve better than to be used as an entertainment 'prop' to amuse The Eagles' fans. "PETA urges Crystal Palace FC to protect animals by retiring Phoenix and committing never to use a live animal mascot again." Palace has not responded to a Reuters request for comment. PETA said no other UK football club still uses a live animal mascot. Some other European clubs have used live eagle mascots, including Portuguese side Benfica and Italian club Lazio.

item.title: UK regulator ends Home REIT investigation
item.description: Britain's financial regulator has closed its two-year investigation into London-listed Home REIT , a British social housing company, although the watchdog said on Wednesday that it supported an ongoing criminal investigation.
item.dc:creator: Kirstin Ridley
item.content:encoded: Britain's financial regulator has closed its two-year investigation into London-listed Home REIT (HOMEH.L) , a British social housing company, although the watchdog said on Wednesday that it supported an ongoing criminal investigation. The Financial Conduct Authority ended the probe without taking any action, helping send the company's beleaguered shares 3.7% higher at the market close, their biggest daily percentage gain since June. "We have carefully considered the case and believe the best way forward is to support the Serious Fraud Office's ongoing investigation," an FCA spokesperson said. The watchdog is reserving its rights to review its decision if new information comes to light. Home REIT's Chair Michael O'Donnell said the FCA investigation was closed following the company's "extensive cooperation". The UK Serious Fraud Office, however, [USN:L8N3YF1AO TEXT:"arrested"] six people in January in an estimated £300 million ($401 million) bribery and fraud investigation. Seven sites were searched, including a home in the Italian city of Venice. Home REIT, which listed on the London Stock Exchange in 2020, bought properties across Britain, raising more than £850 million in its first three years of trading. The company told investors their funds would help to buy and restore properties that would be block-let to publicly funded charities and community interest companies to house rough sleepers, veterans and people struggling with addiction. Rent payments would generate returns for investors. But a report by short-seller Viceroy Research in November 2022 raised concerns that included the valuation of the properties and the ability of the tenants to pay rent. The company [USN:L4N32Q1IW TEXT:"rejected"] the allegations, but its shares were temporarily suspended from trading in January 2023. More than 800 investors are [USN:L8N45N122 TEXT:"suing"] Home REIT, alleging they were misled about the security of the company's rental income, its financial strength and its stated social impact. ($1 = 0.7474 pounds)

item.title: Vers une reprise des discussions trilatérales entre USA, Russie et Ukraine
item.description: La Russie a accepté la proposition des Etats-Unis d'organiser une réunion trilatérale au niveau technique avec l'Ukraine, a déclaré mercredi un représentant américain, tandis que le président ukrainien Volodimir Zelensky a dit soutenir cette démarche et vouloir que les discussions se tiennent au plus tôt.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La Russie a accepté la proposition des Etats-Unis d'organiser une réunion trilatérale au niveau technique avec l'Ukraine, a déclaré mercredi un représentant américain, tandis que le président ukrainien Volodimir Zelensky a dit soutenir cette démarche et vouloir que les discussions se tiennent au plus tôt. Ces commentaires ont été effectués à la suite d'une visite en Russie de Steve Witkoff, émissaire spécial du président américain Donald Trump, lors de laquelle il a rencontré le président russe Vladimir Poutine. Ils s'inscrivent dans un contexte d'inquiétudes à Kyiv et parmi ses alliés à propos d'un possible virage entrepris par Washington au détriment de l'Ukraine, alors que les Etats-Unis ont un temps suspendu le partage de renseignements avec les autorités ukrainiennes à propos des bombardements de la Russie. Donald Trump a également annoncé plus tôt ce mois-ci être convenu lors d'un entretien téléphonique avec Vladimir Poutine d'un accord sur des [USN:L8N45V1O6 TEXT:"livraisons de diesel"], ce qui a provoqué un tollé de la part de responsables ukrainiens et européens ainsi que d'élus démocrates et républicains au Congrès américain. Le Kremlin a fait savoir mercredi que Vladimir Poutine a accepté de reprendre les efforts de paix chapeautés par les Etats-Unis pour mettre fin à la guerre, entrée en février dernier dans sa cinquième année. Ces discussions trilatérales au niveau technique pourraient avoir lieu à Abou Dhabi, qui a déjà accueilli un précédent cycle de pourparlers, et se focaliseraient sur des garanties sécuritaires apportées à la Russie et à l'Ukraine une fois la guerre terminée, a ajouté la présidence russe. Elles pourraient se tenir autour du 10 novembre, a-t-elle indiqué. Volodimir Zelensky a dit par la suite que Kyiv soutenait la proposition de Washington et souhaitait au plus vite une rencontre entre des négociateurs des trois pays. "Le camp américain nous propose de tenir (cette réunion) dès que possible et nous y sommes favorables", a dit le président ukrainien à des journalistes au cours d'un échange via la messagerie WhatsApp, ajoutant avoir été informé par des représentants américains que la Russie "soutenait" l'idée. Les Américains "vont tout faire pour garantir que la réunion se tienne au plus vite, en novembre, je pense au plus tard début novembre", a-t-il ajouté. NEUVIÈME RENCONTRE WITKOFF-POUTINE EN RUSSIE Volodimir Zelensky, qui s'était entretenu mardi avec Steve Witkoff lors d'une réunion en Norvège à laquelle ont également pris part des responsables européens, a souligné que Kyiv soutenait "toute proposition de cessez-le-feu, pour mettre fin à la guerre, des trêves énergétiques". Il avait répété plus tôt être [USN:L6N4670YO TEXT:"disposé à dialoguer"]. Aucun cycle de pourparlers trilatéraux n'a été organisé depuis le début de la guerre entre les Etats-Unis et l'Iran, le 28 février dernier. Quelques jours plus tôt, à Abou Dhabi, les délégations ukrainienne et russe étaient convenues d'un [USN:L8N3Z113X TEXT:"échange de prisonniers"], sans avancer toutefois sur les principaux points de contentieux. Revenu au pouvoir à la Maison blanche en janvier 2025, Donald Trump avait promis de mettre fin à la guerre en Ukraine en "seulement vingt-quatre heures". Il a rétabli les contacts directs avec Moscou, rompus par son prédécesseur Joe Biden en raison du conflit, et pris part l'an dernier à un [USN:L8N3U8008 TEXT:"sommet bilatéral"] avec Vladimir Poutine n'ayant débouché sur aucune mesure de paix. Les positions de l'Ukraine et de la Russie demeurent très éloignées sur les contours d'un potentiel accord. Alors que Volodimir Zelensky écarte l'idée d'abandonner tout territoire ukrainien à Moscou, Vladimir Poutine exige le plein contrôle de la région de Donetsk dans l'Est ukrainien, la garantie que Kyiv n'intégrera pas l'Otan et des restrictions sur les capacités militaires ukrainiennes. Donald Trump, qui s'en était vivement pris à Volodimir Zelensky lors d'une rencontre à la Maison blanche en février 2025, a déclaré cette semaine qu'il serait opportun que l'Ukraine se trouve un nouvel interlocuteur pour négocier et qu'il était temps de mettre fin à la guerre avant que "de mauvaises choses se passent". Steve Witkoff a rencontré mercredi Vladimir Poutine pour la neuvième fois en tant qu'émissaire spécial. Leur réunion, au Grand palais impérial de Saint-Pétersbourg, a duré près de trois heures. Elle a donné lieu notamment à ce qui a été présenté comme un "geste de bonne volonté" de la part du président russe: la libération du ressortissant américain [USN:L6N4670TT TEXT:"Stephen Hubbard"], emprisonné en Russie depuis 2022. Kirill Dmitriev, conseiller spécial du Kremlin qui a également pris part aux discussions, a déclaré que d'importants projets économiques communs ont été évoqués.

item.title: Nestle, Zydus, Abbott face India scrutiny over claims on children's products
item.description: India's food safety regulator issued notices to Nestle India , Zydus Wellness , Abbott Healthcare and others on Wednesday over promotional claims involving products for infants and children that it said breached rules.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: India's food safety regulator issued notices to Nestle India (NEST.NS) , Zydus Wellness (ZYDS.NS) , Abbott Healthcare and others on Wednesday over promotional claims involving products for infants and children that it said breached rules. The action comes days after the regulator [USN:L6N46302P TEXT:"proposed"] banning the addition of sucrose and fructose to foods for infants up to six months old, as India steps up scrutiny of food safety and pushes for front-of-pack warning labels, rattling the country's more than $100 billion packaged food industry. The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India said it issued notices over products including Complan, Lactogen Pro 1 Powder, NAN Excella Pro Stage 1 and infant milk substitutes. The regulator asked Nestle India to provide evidence supporting claims about digestive and immune-system benefits for its Lactogen Pro 1 Powder and NAN Excella Pro Stage 1 infant formula products. Nestle India said FSSAI's latest post reiterated issues raised on September 18 concerning product labels, and that it had already submitted a detailed response to the regulator. Zydus Wellness was asked to provide scientific justification for claims promoting its Complan children's drink, including the tagline "grow taller, faster. clinically proven 2X growth." The company did not immediately respond to requests for comment outside regular business hours. FSSAI also issued notices to social media influencer Ira Fathima and companies including Abbott Healthcare and Nestle India over an Instagram reel promoting infant milk substitutes. An Abbott spokesperson said the company was not involved in or aware of the social media content referenced by the FSSAI notice and became aware of the content only after receiving the regulator's notice. "Abbott does not endorse the claims or representations contained in the content," the spokesperson said. The company added that it had shared this information with the regulator.

item.title: Activos en Brasil se mueven atentos a balotaje; peso mexicano cae con fuerza
item.description: Los activos brasileños cotizaron con bajas el miércoles, atentos a sondeos de intención de voto de cara al esperado y reñido balotaje presidencial del domingo, mientras que el peso mexicano fue golpeado por el desmantelamiento de posiciones de "carry trade", según analistas.
item.dc:creator: Manuel Farías
item.content:encoded: Los activos brasileños cotizaron con bajas el miércoles, atentos a sondeos de intención de voto de cara al esperado y reñido balotaje presidencial del domingo, mientras que el peso mexicano fue golpeado por el desmantelamiento de posiciones de "carry trade", según analistas. * Los mercados bursátiles de la región también reaccionaron a los reportes corporativos del tercer trimestre. * A nivel global, el dólar cayó ligeramente mientras los inversores ya comienzan a mirar de reojo la reunión de política monetaria de la Reserva Federal de la próxima semana. Los mercados descuentan que el banco central mantendrá los costos del crédito, pero esperan un endurecimiento monetario en diciembre. * Mientras, Wall Street avanzó en medio de resultados de firmas ligadas a la inteligencia artificial y el retorno de los bonos del Tesoro retrocedió. Los precios del petróleo cerraron con pocos cambios tras perder el impulso de más temprano cuando escalaron más de 2 dólares por barril. * El real brasileño cedió un 0,18% a 5,0272 por dólar, luego de tres sesiones de avances; al tiempo que el referencial bursátil Bovespa (.BVSP) bajó preliminarmente un 0,92% a 206.379 puntos, al perder impulso tras superar las 209.000 unidades en la apertura después de conocerse un sondeo sobre el balotaje presidencial del domingo. * El Bovespa escaló más de un 1% en la ronda previa, con datos mostrando el ingreso de flujos de inversores extranjeros al mercado. * La ventaja del senador Flávio Bolsonaro sobre el presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva se ha reducido de cara a la segunda vuelta, reveló el miércoles una encuesta de Quaest. * El senador de derecha obtendría el 45% de los votos, frente al 44% del actual mandatario de izquierda. El sondeo anterior de Quaest, de hace una semana, mostró una ventaja de 46% a 44% en favor de Bolsonaro. * Las encuestas muestran que el senador mantiene una ventaja sobre el presidente de cara al balotaje, aunque la distancia se ha reducido y se estima que la elección será muy reñida. Bolsonaro ganó la primera vuelta pese a que la mayoría de los sondeos daban como triunfador a Lula. * El peso mexicano bajó un 1,4%, a 18,6714 unidades por dólar, un mínimo del año, afectado por la reducción del diferencial de tasas de interés con Estados Unidos. * El índice S&P/BMV IPC (.MXX) , integrado por las 35 acciones más líquidas del mercado, trepó un 1,43%, a 70.249,54 puntos, en su quinta sesión de alzas consecutiva apuntalado por resultados corporativos del tercer trimestre. * "El peso mexicano es la divisa más depreciada en la sesión, debido a que continúa el desmantelamiento de posiciones de carry trade, ante la reducción del diferencial de tasas de interés entre México y Estados Unidos. Este diferencial se redujo a 250 puntos base desde el 16 de septiembre, cuando la Reserva Federal incrementó su tasa de interés en 25 puntos base", dijo Banco Base en un reporte. * Los mercados anticipan una nueva alza del costo del crédito en diciembre por parte de la Fed, mientras que en México no se descarta una reducción del costo del crédito durante el próximo año. * El peso colombiano cerró con caída de un 0,50% a 3.190 unidades por dólar, después de que el Gobierno anunció que fijará por decreto el presupuesto de gastos para 2027, luego de que el proyecto de ley aprobado por el Congreso se hundió por un vicio de trámite, generando incertidumbre sobre la distribución del gasto público en medio de persistentes presiones fiscales. * En la bolsa, el índice accionario COLCAP (.COLCAP) se valorizó un 1,08% a 2.560,52 puntos. * El peso chileno , cerró la jornada con una caída del 0,41%, en 978,20/978,50 unidades por dólar, en línea con sus pares de la región, mientras que el principal índice de la bolsa de comercio de Santiago, el IPSA (.SPIPSA) , avanzó un 0,55%, a 10.987,14 puntos. * El peso mayorista argentino se depreció un leve 0,07% a 1.526 unidades por dólar, junto a contratos de futuros equilibrados e intervención del banco central (BCRA) para acumular reservas a favor de sus arcas. La entidad monetaria compró 46 millones de dólares del mercado cambiario. * Mientras, el índice líder MSCI Merval (.MMXMRVLGA) de la bolsa de Buenos Aires escaló un 1,68%, luego de acumular tres jornadas en baja. * La moneda peruana, el sol , finalizó con una caída de 0,23% a 3,4340/3,4350 unidades por dólar. Por su parte, la Bolsa de Lima (.MXNUAMPESCPGPE) retrocedió un 0,31% a 1.574,24 puntos.

item.title: Five AI quirks and conundrums to watch this earnings season
item.description: As US earnings season gets underway, AI bulls and bears are becoming more entrenched in their positions. Several market quirks, curiosities and anomalies have popped up that underscore these extremes.
item.dc:creator: Jamie McGeever
item.content:encoded: As [USN:L8N4611ZZ TEXT:"US earnings season"] gets underway, [USN:L6N45T17Q TEXT:"AI"] bulls and bears are becoming more entrenched in their positions. Several market quirks, curiosities and anomalies have popped up that underscore these extremes. This shouldn't come as a surprise, because, when it comes to AI, investors and analysts are largely flying blind. The technology is in its infancy, is evolving at breakneck speed, and has potential powers that are almost unfathomable. And the cost of funding this revolution? It's almost unfathomable too. The implications for the broader market are also enormous. According to JPMorgan Private Bank's Michael Cembalest, AI-related stocks, a group he narrows down to 41 names, have accounted for 75% of S&P 500 (.SPX) returns, 80% of earnings growth and 90% of capital spending growth since ChatGPT launched in November 2022. The results and outlooks from hyperscalers, “neoclouds”, chipmakers, software providers and all the AI-adjacent firms will set the tone for Wall Street and global markets going into next year. Here's the backdrop: Equity-bond gap As the old saying goes, bond investors are paid to be bearish and equity investors are paid to be bullish. Perhaps that helps explain why many of the bonds issued to finance America's record-breaking AI investment are trading at such weak levels even as AI-related shares mostly continue to move higher. Amid the latest wave of market jitters, it's easy to forget that the S&P 500 and Nasdaq (.IXIC) were at record highs only two weeks ago. Those jitters have been meaningful, of course. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (.SOX) is down 25% from its June peak, and earlier this year the S&P 500 software index (.SPLRCIS) was down 35% from its record high. But the third-quarter earnings season begins, the chip index is up 55% year to date and software stocks have climbed back into positive territory for the year. While “neocloud” company CoreWeave (CRWV.O) shares are down 13% this year, its October 2031 bond has plunged more than 20% since its launch in April and is trading in distressed territory below 80 cents on the dollar. Meanwhile, credit default swap spreads, which measure the cost of insuring against bond default, have recently soared to record highs for AI borrowers including CoreWeave and Oracle (ORCL.N) , and even for trillion-dollar giants Amazon (AMZN.O) , Alphabet (GOOGL.O) and Meta (META.O) . Someone might want to remind investors that debt is still senior to equity. CoreWeave: stock and awe? [USN:L4N461208 TEXT:"CoreWeave"] is at the center of the latest market maelstrom. The Nvidia-backed (NVDA.O) AI infrastructure firm is loss-making, heavily indebted and faces soaring borrowing costs. But Wall Street analysts have wildly different views about its prospects. Analysts at HSBC this week published an extremely gloomy note, forecasting average returns through 2030 below CoreWeave’s cost of borrowing. "The more the company invests with this return profile, the more the value destruction," they wrote. Investors should cut their holdings of the stock, HSBC advised, assigning it a target price of only $39, some 37% below Tuesday’s close around $62. Seems pretty clear-cut, right? Maybe not. Looking at the same data, equity strategists at Goldman Sachs this week raised their recommendation on the stock to a “buy” from “neutral.” They reckon annual recurring revenue per megawatt is likely to rise over the next 24 months, and argue that the recent surge in yields doesn't represent the firm's true cost of borrowing because most of its financing is asset-backed. Even though they cut their price target to $106 from $139, that still represents upside of around 70%. Token gesture Growth in token spending is slowing, yet token usage continues to soar. Tokens are units of data processed by AI models during training and inference, and they essentially reflect the strength of demand for "compute". Slowing growth or outright declines in prices would indicate companies are reluctant to pay for that compute unless they can turn it into "higher top-line growth, bigger profit margins or substantial cost savings," according to Apollo's Torsten Slok. These benefits have yet to materialize. But token usage is still rising strongly and steadily. So demand is still there. It's just that spending appears to have topped out because token prices have fallen, which is a reminder to investors that revenue at the big AI model developers like OpenAI and [USN:L4N4661JI TEXT:"Anthropic"] may not continue to rise as spectacularly as hoped. AI stocks are highly sensitive to expectations about future AI use and, obviously, revenue. How long can investors ignore the gap between the two? Cold storage Vast sums are being spent to address the shortage of computing power, but apparently some of that power simply cannot be switched on. Quite literally. Energy supply-chain chokepoints, including insufficient electricity and inadequate grid connections, mean many AI chips are sitting and depreciating in warehouses. Only this week, Microsoft (MSFT.O) [USN:L6N464023 TEXT:"pulled out of a deal"] to anchor a flagship data center in Britain with Nvidia-backed Nscale after electricity grid officials said they did not expect to supply power to the site until the 2030s. Morgan Stanley analysts now reckon US data center developers will face a 30% to 40% power shortfall through 2028, equivalent to 34% of total chip demand. Demand for power is rising, but it can't come online quickly enough. Revenue conundrum Ultimately, the AI investment bet hinges on whether the extraordinary sums being borrowed and spent on the technology will pay off. Third-quarter earnings won't give a definitive answer, but every nod and steer will be seized upon. The sums are eye-watering. McKinsey and S&P Global estimate that the top six US hyperscalers alone will spend more than $7 trillion on data centers and other AI-related capital expenditure between 2025 and 2030. Columbia University's Stijn Van Nieuwerburgh reckons the cost of financing the AI buildout from last year to 2032 will be $10.3 trillion . This spending is highly concentrated — just 2% of firms account for over 50% of total spending, according to one study . If these firms want a conservative 10% return on that outlay, Van Nieuwerburgh estimates that annual revenue will need to be around $3.55 trillion by 2032. Some analysts suggest annual revenue of over $4 trillion will be needed to make the investment pay off. That's over 10% of expected GDP in 2032. That’s a very, very high bar.
